extracted.intended_audience: Harvard SEAS researchers, faculty, staff, and communications contacts preparing press releases
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for preparing and evaluating press releases about research, events, awards, or institutional changes aimed at media and non-technical readers. Emphasizes newsworthiness criteria, production details, and coordination with communications offices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Press release length and audience
rubrics_metrics.description: "Press releases, typically 600-800 word summaries written for a non-technical reader" distributed to media to highlight newsworthy activities, events, or institutional changes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keep releases concise (around 600–800 words) and target a non-technical/general-audience style suitable for journalists and the broader public.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scientific/Practical Impact
rubrics_metrics.description: Does the research have major scientific implications or practical applications?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate whether the work advances its field substantially or offers clear real-world benefits that would interest a broad audience or specialized media.

rubrics_metrics.name: News Hook
rubrics_metrics.description: Is there something broad-based that journalists might find compelling?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify a clear, timely angle (surprising result, human-interest connection, policy relevance, large-scale impact) that makes the story attractive to reporters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quality Standards
rubrics_metrics.description: Is the research groundbreaking, original, and timely?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess novelty and rigor; prioritize work that represents a clear advance or timely contribution rather than incremental results.

rubrics_metrics.name: Uniqueness
rubrics_metrics.description: Is the work unusual or unexpected in nature?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Highlight aspects that distinguish the work from typical studies (unexpected findings, novel methods, counterintuitive conclusions) to increase newsworthiness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Visual Assets
rubrics_metrics.description: Do you have engaging or beautiful accompanying photos, movies, etc.?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide high-quality, relevant visuals (images, video, graphics) that help journalists and audiences quickly understand and promote the story.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commercial Interest
rubrics_metrics.description: Is there a patent pending or collaboration with industry?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note translational or commercial aspects (patents, startups, industry partnerships) which can increase media interest and require coordination with tech transfer/commercialization offices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Award Recognition
rubrics_metrics.description: Is the award considered "major" (Nobel, NAE, etc.)?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prioritize coverage for high-profile honors; specify the stature of awards when evaluating whether a press release is warranted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication Considerations
rubrics_metrics.description: Verify the journal's embargo policy and whether it issues its own press releases or promotes authors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check journal embargoes and communications plans before publicizing results; coordinate timing and messaging to avoid conflicts with publishers' policies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Collaborative Coordination
rubrics_metrics.description: If the work is collaborative, discuss the possibility with colleagues and coordinate with the SEAS Communications Office to align efforts with other institutions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When multiple institutions or labs are involved, agree on messaging, timing, and lead contacts; coordinate with institutional communications teams to present a unified story and avoid duplicate or conflicting releases.
